How an rProject Project Works

Ivan Jacob Agaloos Pesigan

Source: vignettes/structure.Rmd
structure.Rmd

Every project is an R project built from the rProject template: a CRAN package, a manuscript, a library of references, a talk, or a container image. This vignette describes how such a project is laid out, which files make writes, and how a change travels from Overleaf to the public repository. It is written for the user, for co-authors, and for AI agents.

Types

The type is a line in .setup/scripts/project.R, for example type <- "cran". Each type uses a few sets of template files (inst/template/<set>/).

type sets use
rProject common, package, cran, rproject rProject itself
cran common, package, cran R packages (cran-, devel-)
man common, package, man manuscripts (man*), which are R packages too
lib common, lib biblatex libraries (lib-*)
talk common, talk talks
docker docker container images (docker-*)

Folders

The standard folders, the types that have them, and what they are for (inst/template/folders.tsv). Private folders stay on Overleaf and in the private repository; they never go public. make creates the folders marked “created” (with an empty .gitignore); the others appear when they are needed. make tree lists the folders of a project and flags the ones that are missing or not standard for its type.

folder types private created purpose
R/ rProject, cran, man package functions, one per file
tests/testthat/ rProject, cran, man unit tests, one file per function
man/ rProject, cran, man help pages, generated by roxygen (never edit)
data/ rProject, cran, man package data (.rda), written by the scripts in .setup/data-process/
inst/ rProject, cran, man files installed with the package (CITATION, …)
src/ rProject, cran, man C++ sources, copied from .setup/cpp/ by Build()
vignettes/ rProject, cran, man, talk vignettes; those with a source in .setup/vignettes/ are generated
.github/workflows/ all CI workflows, written by Template() (change them in rProject’s inst/template/)
.sim/ rProject, cran, man, talk simulation scripts (SLURM, GNU Parallel); a simulation has .sim/README.md
.sif/ man, talk Apptainer images or links to them (local only; never uploaded)
scripts/ docker the image’s install scripts; scripts/setup.sh runs them in order
detritus/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk LaTeX by-products (the .tex knitted from .Rtex)
.library/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk the project’s R library (local only)
.verify/ all a clone of the private repository, to check pushes (local only)
quarto/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk the rendered Quarto site (Quarto())
.quarto/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk Quarto’s cache (local only)
pkgdown/ rProject, cran, man, talk the rendered pkgdown site (Site())
.claude/ all yes Claude Code’s project settings
.setup/scripts/ all project.R (the project’s settings) and the make scripts
.setup/repo/ all yes where the project lives: private and public repository, Overleaf project
.setup/ai/ all yes specs, the plan, the handoff, project.md
.setup/logs/ all yes one log per Overleaf push, and index.md
.setup/notes/ all yes notes and files: claude.txt (resume commands); lib-* keep the reference PDFs here
.setup/todo/ all yes todo.txt, the user’s to-do list, and its attachments
.setup/readme/ all README.Rmd, the source of README.md
.setup/latex/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk LaTeX sources (.Rtex), preamble/, r-scripts/, bib/, tikz/, sty/, equations/, slides/; pdf/ and figures/ are generated
.setup/quarto/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk Quarto site sources
.setup/load/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk load.R, which loads the project for knitr and Quarto
.setup/pkgdown/ rProject, cran, man, talk _pkgdown.yml
.setup/vignettes/ rProject, cran, man, talk yes vignette sources that are precompiled (*.Rmd.orig)
.setup/build/ rProject, cran, man yes the package tarball and the PDF manual (Build(), Manual())
.setup/cpp/ rProject, cran, man yes C++ sources, copied into src/
.setup/r-dependencies/ rProject, cran, man yes R functions shared with other packages, copied into R/
.setup/r-miscellaneous/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk yes helpers that are not part of the package (for example texTools)
.setup/tests-benchmark/ rProject, cran, man yes benchmark tests, outside the unit tests (test-benchmark-<pkg>-<name>.R)
.setup/tests-external/ rProject, cran, man yes external tests, outside the unit tests (test-external-<pkg>-<name>.R)
.setup/data-raw/ rProject, man yes shareable raw data
.setup/data-process/ rProject, man yes scripts that build data/*.rda from the raw data
.setup/data-analysis/ rProject, man yes analysis scripts and their output
.setup/data-dependencies/ rProject, man yes .rda files loaded for knitr and Quarto
.setup/data-private/ rProject, man yes restricted data: never public
.setup/data-external/ rProject, man yes data from elsewhere (the source is recorded in the data manifest)
.setup/data-cache/ rProject, man yes cached downloads and intermediate data
.setup/bin/ rProject, cran, man, lib, talk, docker optional: R scripts run at make project (for example, to build a bespoke binary)

Notes:

  • .setup/notes/ is private. Library projects keep the reference PDFs there.
  • .setup/bin/ is optional: Binary() runs its R scripts at make project (for example, to build a bespoke binary).
  • Code coverage: to leave files out, put covr’s .covrignore at the project root and add it to .Rbuildignore (ignore in .setup/scripts/project.R).
  • The naming rules for files in R/, tests/testthat/, .setup/r-dependencies/, and the test folders are in the R style guide (.setup/latex/rProject-002-style-R.Rtex).

Template files

rProject::Template() (run by make project and make template) keeps the template files of a project in step with rProject. Each file has a tier:

  • Tier 1, links. Files that Overleaf or make needs (Makefile, latexmkrc, the LaTeX preamble, …). They are linked into the Overleaf project from rProject’s Overleaf project. Template() never writes them; it lists those that differ as links to refresh.
  • Tier 2, written by make. Everything else: the workflows, the make scripts, the Quarto pages, the folder skeleton. Template() writes a file that is missing or differs (the template wins: change it in rProject). These files are not uploaded to Overleaf.

Workflows that only some projects run are in a catalog (inst/template/workflows/). A project names the ones it runs in project.R:

workflows <- c("docker-build-push-multi", "docker-build-push-daily-multi")
workflow_daily <- "docs"
workflow_title <- "Docker Build and Push Docs [multi] (Daily)"
workflow_cron <- "30 3 * * *"

The daily docker workflow is written as docker-build-push-daily-multi-<workflow_daily>.yml, with its title and cron filled in.

Files that leave the template are listed in inst/template/removed.tsv. Template() deletes them (a folder only when nothing but .gitignore files is left in it) and names them, so that they can be deleted in Overleaf too.

From Overleaf to the public repository

  1. Edit on Overleaf. Overleaf is the main editor. Co-authors edit there. Agents edit a local clone; the user uploads the changed files.
  2. Log. Every change set (one Overleaf push) has a log in .setup/logs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md (make log), with the commit message and the files to upload or delete.
  3. O2G. The user pushes from Overleaf to the private GitHub repository. make verify RECORD=TRUE checks that the private repository matches the local clone and records the push in the log and in .setup/logs/index.md.
  4. PUB. make all builds and checks everything; make auto checks the public export (no private files, nothing over 50 MB, no tokens) and pushes to the public repository.

Make targets

Target Does
make project settings, template files, AI files
make all build, docs, LaTeX, pkgdown, Quarto, coverage
make lint style and lint the R code; report Overleaf limits
make sizecheck check Overleaf limits
make spec TOPIC=<topic> start a spec for a change set
make log TOPIC=<topic> SUMMARY="..." write the change-set log
make verify RECORD=TRUE verify and record a push from Overleaf
make auto publish to the public repository
make tree the project’s folders and what each is for
make template write the template files only
make latex, make pdf knit and compile the LaTeX sources

R runs only inside an Apptainer image: apptainer exec <image> make <target>.

Keywords

Short messages from the user to an AI agent:

Keyword Means
“O2G” the user pushed from Overleaf to GitHub: verify and record the push
“PUB” the user ran make all and make auto: check the public repository and its CI
“build docs” publish the docker images in order and rebuild the docs images
“EX” the user is leaving: update .setup/notes/claude.txt and the handoff
“handoff” rewrite .setup/ai/handoff.md without leaving

The private files that agents read (AGENTS.md, .setup/ai/) are written by rProject::AI().
